content: 1. The relative risk of developing probable dementia when using conjugated estrogens plus medroxyprogesterone acetate (CE/MPA) compared to placebo was 2.05 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21 to 3.48). 2. The absolute risk of developing probable dementia with CE/MPA was 45 cases per 10,000 women-years, compared to 22 cases per 10,000 women-years in the placebo group. 3. Among the cases of probable dementia in the CE/MPA group, 82% occurred in women older than 70 years. 4. The most common classification of probable dementia in both the estrogen plus progestin group and the placebo group was Alzheimer’s disease. 5. When data from the estrogen-alone and estrogen-plus-progestin WHIMS (Women’s Health Initiative Memory Study) substudies were pooled as planned in the WHIMS protocol, the overall relative risk for probable dementia was 1.76 (95% CI, 1.19 to 2.60). 6. Since both substudies were conducted in women aged 65 to 79 years, it is unknown whether these findings apply to younger postmenopausal women. Gender 7. The FDA has not provided specific guidance on the use of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate with respect to specific gender populations. Race 8. The FDA has not provided specific guidance on the use of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate with respect to specific racial populations. Renal Impairment 9. The FDA has not provided specific guidance on the use of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in patients with renal impairment. Hepatic Impairment 10. The FDA has not provided specific guidance on the use of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in patients with hepatic impairment. Females of Reproductive Potential and Males 11. The FDA has not provided specific guidance on the use of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in women of reproductive potential or in males. Immunocompromised Patients 12. The FDA has not provided specific guidance on the use of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in immunocompromised patients. Administration and Monitoring Administration Secondary Amenorrhea 13. Medroxyprogesterone acetate tablets may be administered in doses of 5 or 10 mg daily for 5 to 10 days. 14. To induce an optimal secretory transformation of an endometrium that has been adequately primed with either endogenous or exogenous estrogen, a dose of 10 mg daily for 10 days is recommended. 15. Therapy for secondary amenorrhea may be initiated at any time. 16. Progestin withdrawal bleeding typically occurs within 3 to 7 days after discontinuing medroxyprogesterone acetate therapy. Abnormal Uterine Bleeding Due to Hormonal Imbalance in the Absence of Organic Pathology 17. Starting on the calculated 16th or 21st day of the menstrual cycle, 5 or 10 mg of medroxyprogesterone acetate may be administered daily for 5 to 10 days. 18. To achieve optimal secretory transformation of an endometrium adequately primed with estrogen, 10 mg daily for 10 days beginning on the 16th day of the cycle is suggested. 19. Progestin withdrawal bleeding usually occurs within 3 to 7 days after discontinuing therapy. 20. Patients with a history of recurrent abnormal uterine bleeding may benefit from planned menstrual cycling with medroxyprogesterone acetate. Reduction of Endometrial Hyperplasia in Postmenopausal Women Receiving Daily 0.625 mg Conjugated Estrogens 21. When estrogen is prescribed for a postmenopausal woman with a uterus, a progestin should also be initiated to reduce the risk of endometrial cancer. 22. A woman without a uterus does not require progestin. 23. Estrogen, alone or in combination with a progestin, should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals and risks for the individual woman. 24. Patients should be re-evaluated periodically (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) to determine if treatment is still necessary. 25. 26. Medroxyprogesterone acetate tablets may be administered in doses of 5 or 10 mg daily for 12 to 14 consecutive days per month in postmenopausal women receiving daily 0.625 mg conjugated estrogens, either beginning on the 1st day of the cycle or the 16th day of the cycle. 27. Patients should be started at the lowest dose. 28. The lowest effective dose of medroxyprogesterone acetate has not been determined. Monitoring 29. There is limited information regarding the monitoring of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in the drug label. IV Compatibility 30. There is limited information regarding the IV compatibility of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in the drug label. Overdosage 31. Overdosage of estrogen plus progestin therapy may cause nausea, vomiting, breast tenderness, dizziness, abdominal pain, drowsiness/fatigue, and withdrawal bleeding in women. 32. Treatment of overdose involves discontinuation of CE/MPA and the institution of appropriate symptomatic care. Pharmacology Mechanism of Action 33. Medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA), when administered orally or parenterally in recommended doses to women with adequate endogenous estrogen, transforms proliferative endometrium into secretory endometrium. 34. Androgenic and anabolic effects have been observed, but the drug appears to lack significant estrogenic activity. 35. Parenterally administered MPA inhibits gonadotropin production, preventing follicular maturation and ovulation; however, this effect does not occur with the usual recommended oral dosage given as single daily doses. Structure 36. Medroxyprogesterone acetate tablets contain medroxyprogesterone acetate, a derivative of progesterone. 37. It is a white to off-white, odorless crystalline powder, stable in air, with a melting point between 200 and 210°C. 38. It is freely soluble in chloroform, soluble in acetone and dioxane, sparingly soluble in alcohol and methanol, slightly soluble in ether, and insoluble in water. 39. The chemical name for medroxyprogesterone acetate is pregn-4-ene-3,20-dione, 17-(acetyloxy)-6-methyl-, (6α)-. 40. Each tablet for oral administration contains 2.5 mg, 5 mg, or 10 mg of medroxyprogesterone acetate, USP. 41. In addition, each tablet contains the following inactive ingredients: crospovidone, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, methylcellulose, pregelatinized starch, and sodium lauryl sulfate. Pharmacodynamics 42. There is limited information regarding the pharmacodynamics of oral medroxyprogesterone acetate in the drug label. Pharmacokinetics 43. The pharmacokinetics of MPA were determined in 20 postmenopausal women following a single-dose administration of eight 2.5 mg medroxyprogesterone acetate tablets or a single administration of two 10 mg medroxyprogesterone acetate tablets under fasting conditions. 44. In another study, the steady-state pharmacokinetics of MPA were determined under fasting conditions in 30 postmenopausal women following daily administration of one 10 mg medroxyprogesterone acetate tablet for 7 days. 45. In both studies, MPA was quantified in serum using a validated gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) method. 46. Estimates of the pharmacokinetic parameters of MPA after single and multiple doses of medroxyprogesterone acetate tablets were highly variable. 47. No specific investigation on the absolute bioavailability of MPA in humans has been conducted. 48. MPA is rapidly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, with maximum concentrations achieved between 2 to 4 hours after oral administration.
